newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Gulf gasoline shoots up late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Gulf gasoline shoots up late.

text.p: U.S. Gulf prompt conventional gasoline skyrocketed higher late Tuesday as refiners buying drove differentials higher, though little action was seen in the Midcontinent or New York Harbor.
On the NYMEX, June gasoline gained 0.18 cent to settle at 65.39 cents a gallon, while June heating dipped 0.28 cent to end at 57.64 cents a gallon.

Prompt conventional M1 unleaded gasoline changed hands as high as 1.50 cents under the screen, traders said, up about 2.0 cents from late Monday levels, as refineries bid the market higher in an attempt to cover short positions.
However, the strength was mostly concentrated in the prompt barrels, with M1 for end-of-month delivery changing hands at 2.50 cents under the June NYMEX, nearly 1.00 cent up from Monday.
Aggressive buying interest in the prompt market was caused by refiners seeking barrels ahead of the Colonial Pipeline's scheduling deadline at the end of the day, players said.
"We saw a lot refineries who were short here," one Gulf Coast trader said, "and a lot of people were rolling those short positions forward."
That rolling of short positions is likely to trigger another bullish spike on Friday when the next deadline hits, traders said.
Prompt reformulated gasolines saw little movement during Tuesday's trade, with the market players beginning to shift its attention to the early June barrels.
Differentials saw only modest movement Tuesday, with the prompt 54-grade remaining under pressure, traders said.
Prompt 540-grade jet fuel changed hands at 0.35 cent over the June NYMEX, about 0.15 cent off the levels recorded Monday.
Gasolines remained steady, traders said, with prompt conventional M2 offered at 2.00 cents over the June NYMEX, while prompt A2 reformulated gasoline offered at 1.00 cent over the June futures.

Products were quiet amid a dearth of news as a lack of buyers helped weaken prices. Group Three unleaded differentials were about a quarter cent softer from midday at 6.75/7.00 cents over the June NYMEX, with the re-grade at 2.75/3.00 cents.
Prompt low sulphur differentials were also weaker at 5.50/5.75 cents over NYMEX June heating oil.
The Chicago markets were steady to a tad weaker, traders said,with unleaded differentials remaining 2.50/2.75 cents. Low sulphur was off a quarter cent for the day at 3.50/3.75 cents.
